SM16A-01.bounds: Free: both roots are real and positive (sum 7, product 9, disc 13>0), so r^2 s + rs^2 > 0 - all four options positive. No free magnitude bound exists: pinning the value to 63 requires either Vieta (the declared target insight) or the quadratic formula (the item's work). Order of magnitude is not free because the roots (5.30, 1.70) are not estimable without that work.
issues: key is the largest option; 3 of 22 items in this batch have that, which is not a pattern

SM16A-02.bounds: Reading used: strict. p(-2) = -8 + 4k - 8 - 30 = 4k - 46, but k is unknown without the factor theorem (the target insight), so no free bound follows. Stronger reading: if a solver assumes k is an integer (every other constant in the stem is), 4k - 46 == 2 (mod 4), which kills -44 (0 mod 4) and leaves 3. I did not charge this because nothing in the stem makes k an integer, and the mod-4 step still needs the (-2)^2 = 4 term structure.
issues: -44 dies to a mod-4 argument under an integer-k assumption; 3 survivors under that reading, still not thin

SM16A-03.bounds: Free lower bound: one year loses less than six years, so remaining > 65% (all four pass). Free UPPER bound by monotonicity alone, no exponential arithmetic: under exponential decay the yearly absolute losses are strictly decreasing, so the FIRST year's loss strictly exceeds the six-year average 35/6 = 5.833 points. Hence remaining < 94.167%. That eliminates 94.2% with no use of the sixth-root insight. 83.9% and 91.7% survive: killing either needs the compounding the item tests.
issues: 94.2% is the linear/no-compounding value, which is a strict supremum here - failure mode 2 ('the limiting thing'). It is free-dead. Item still has 3 survivors, so this is recorded, not charged.

SM16A-04.bounds: Free: at x = -4 every term of 3x^2 - 5x + 2 is positive (x^2 > 0, -5x > 0 for x < 0, +2 > 0), so f(-4) > 0. That kills -30 without evaluating anything. I did NOT charge the sharper bound f(-4) > 3*16 = 48 (which would also kill 30), because computing (-4)^2 = 16 is exactly the step the item tests.

SM16A-05.bounds: No free bound. Every route to the sum of x-coordinates (combining into x^2 - 9x + 8, or locating the intersections numerically) is the item's own work. Sign and magnitude of the sum are unconstrained by anything free.
issues: option-set shape: 6, 8, 9 cluster and 29 is a lone outlier, so 29 is cheap to reject on shape alone. Fixable - replace 29 with a clustered wrong value (e.g. 3, the product-of-roots-minus... any value in 1-15 range with a named procedure). This is an options-only tell, flagged for the other half.

SM16A-06.bounds: No free bound. p(-1) = -14 - a and a is pinned only by the remainder theorem (the target insight). Nothing free constrains the sign or size of a remainder; 0 is a legal remainder value a priori.
issues: -19.5 is the only non-integer in the set and 0 is the only 'round' value; both are shape tells visible to an options-only attack. The non-integrality is forced by the mechanism (x-2 read as a factor gives a = 11/2), so it is unavoidable for THAT distractor; it could be avoided by choosing a different wrong procedure.

SM16A-07.bounds: Free: sqrt(3x) requires 3x >= 0, so any solution has x >= 0 and the sum is >= 0. That kills -3 using only the domain of a square root, which is not the tested step. I did NOT charge the stronger bound x >= 6 (from x - 6 = sqrt(...) >= 0), which would also kill 3 and leave 2: that inequality IS the extraneous-root check the item exists to test, so by the stated rule it is not free.

SM16A-08.bounds: Reading used: stronger, and stated. (a) x = 2 makes the printed denominators x - 2 and x^2 - 4 zero. Seeing that requires ZERO algebra - it is read off the page, not produced by clearing denominators - so I count it free even though the subskill names domain rejection. (b) x = 7 dies to a free magnitude bound: for any x > 2, x/(x-2) > 1 and 3/(x+2) > 0, so LHS > 1, while RHS = 8/(x^2-4) = 8/45 < 1. No algebra, just signs and sizes. Survivors: -7 and -5. Under the strict reading (a) is not free and the count is 3.
issues: thin at 2 survivors under the free-inspection reading. Repair: replace '7' with a negative wrong value produced by a named procedure (e.g. -14, the constant term of x^2 + 5x - 14 reported as the root, or -2, the other excluded value) so that the surviving field is not just the key plus one.

SM16A-09.bounds: No free bound. Nothing in the stem forces the solution to be a perfect cube, positive-only, or bounded; each option requires the u-substitution (or a calculator check, which is available on every equation item and is not a bound) to refuse.
issues: shape tell for the options-only half: 8 and 27 are visibly 2^3 and 3^3 while 3 and 19 are not, and the stem asks for the GREATEST. A solver who only notices the cube structure picks 27. Fixable by making a distractor a cube too (e.g. 64 from u = 4 on a mis-factoring) so the cube shape stops selecting.

SM16A-10.bounds: No free bound. The magnitude argument that kills 5 and 13 (f(x) = 2x - 1, so x = 5 gives g = 86 >> 30) runs through the composition, which is the target insight. Sign is unconstrained: the stem asks for the greatest of two branches and -2 is a real branch.
issues: 5 and 13 are weak for anyone who has done ANY of the composition, but they are not free-dead

SM16A-11.bounds: Free: the stated domain x >= 3 is read off the stem, so f-inverse(37) >= 3 and -1 is dead before any algebra. 4 and 19 survive: refusing them requires either the vertex form or evaluating f at them, and evaluating f IS the inverse relation the item tests. Agrees with the author's own count of 3.

SM16A-12.bounds: Reading used: stronger, and stated. The last operation is an explicit subtraction of 5, so min(g) = M - 5 where M is whatever the horizontal shift leaves as the minimum of f(x+2). The only other parameter in the stem is 2. Option 1 requires M = 6 (the minimum RAISED by 10) and option -6 requires M = -1 (raised by 3); no reading of a horizontal shift by 2 - correct (M = -4) or the standard misreading (M = -6 or -2) - produces either. Both are free-dead without using the fact that a horizontal shift preserves the range, which is the target insight. Survivors: -11 (M = -6) and -9 (key). Under the weakest reading ('the -5 cannot raise the minimum') only option 1 dies and the count is 3.
issues: thin at 2. Repair: every distractor must have the -5 actually applied. Concretely replace '1' with -7 (inside +2 misread as a vertical raise, -4 + 2 - 5) and '-6' with -14 (the -5 applied twice, -4 - 5 - 5), giving -14 / -11 / -9 / -7. Check the result for a monotone ladder before shipping - the spacing 3/2/2 with the key third is acceptable but close.

SM16A-13.bounds: Strict reading. The parity bound is real but not free: c = (-3)(2) + (-3)(5) + (2)(5) is even+odd+even = odd, which kills -30 and 4 and leaves 2 - but knowing c is the sum of the PAIRWISE PRODUCTS is verbatim the declared target insight, so by the stated rule it does not reduce the count. Recorded because it is the cheapest half-knowledge route in the batch: a student who knows the shape of Vieta without computing gets to a coin flip between -11 and 31.
issues: parity gives a 2-survivor route to anyone who knows only that c is a sum of three pairwise products. Fixable by choosing zeros that make the wrong Vieta symmetric functions share c's parity (e.g. zeros -3, 2, 4: c = -6 -12 + 8 = -10, sum 3, product -24 - mixed parity no longer separates).

SM16A-14.bounds: No free bound. Both sides are powers of 2 for every real x; separating the options needs 4(x+1) = 6(x-2), which is the item's work. Nothing free fixes the sign or size of x.

SM16A-15.bounds: Free: compounding strictly exceeds simple growth over more than one period, so the answer > 12000 * (1 + 0.06*8) = 17760. That is a convexity bound requiring no evaluation of 1.06^8, and 17760 is exactly the simple-growth value, i.e. it sits ON the infimum. Killing 18044 (1.06^7) needs the 2010-2018 period count, which the subskill names as tested; killing 19042 (1.08^6) needs the actual arithmetic. Both survive.
issues: 17760 is free-dead by the same convexity mechanism as SM16A-03's 94.2%: the linear/no-compounding option is always the infimum or supremum in a compounding item. Two of 22 here. Not charged (3 survivors each) but worth a standing note to authors: the no-compounding value is never a live distractor.

SM16A-16.bounds: DEAD ON A FREE BOUND. The stem states the minimum value of f is 25, so f(t) >= 25 for EVERY t - that is the definition of a minimum, not the item's insight (which is completing the square / the vertex formula). Evaluate at t = -1: f(-1) = 1 - k + 34 = 35 - k >= 25 forces k <= 10, killing 50 and 59 in one line of arithmetic. Evaluate at t = -4: for k = 9, f(-4) = 16 - 36 + 34 = 14 < 25, killing 9. For k = 6, f(-1) = 29 and f(-4) = 26, both >= 25 - the key survives every such probe by construction, because its minimum really is 25. One survivor. A second free bound bites from the other side and confirms it: f(x) = 25 must have a real solution (the minimum is attained), so x^2 + kx + 9 = 0 has real roots and k >= 6 by discriminant. The free window is 6 <= k <= 10 and a single evaluation inside it closes to k = 6.
issues: The author certified this item at >= 3 survivors. It is 1. The mechanism generalises: on a 'given the minimum value, find the coefficient' stem, EVERY distractor with a larger k has a true minimum below 25 and is therefore refutable by one substitution - so no 4-option version of this stem survives unless every distractor is SMALLER than the key, and those are refutable only through the discriminant bound, which is also free.

Repair is not a swap of two options: the free window 6 <= k <= 10 contains no usable distractor (9 and 10 both die to one evaluation). Recommended rebuild: ask for something the minimum does not expose pointwise - e.g. give f(x) = x^2 + kx + 34 with k > 0 and state that the minimum occurs at x = -3, asking for the minimum VALUE (options then are function values, and f(t) >= min gives no leverage); or keep the current question but make the answer a non-integer so that a single-point probe cannot cleanly separate. If the item ships as-is, it is a free item for any solver who tries one substitution.

SM16A-17.bounds: Free: |x-3| <= 11 and |x+2| <= 11 give -8 <= x <= 14; all four options are inside. The triangle-inequality floor (the sum is always >= 5) and the constant-on-[-2,3] fact are the case analysis the item tests, so I did not charge them. Direct substitution refutes 1, 5 and 8.5, but substitution is available on every solve-for-x item and is not a bound - see the batch-level note.
issues: 8.5 is the only non-integer and 1 the only option below 3 - shape tells for the options-only half, not bound defects

SM16L-01.bounds: No free bound. Neither variable is constrained in sign, so the usual 5(x+y) <= 6x+5y <= 6(x+y) sandwich is unavailable; recovering x+y = 9 requires adding the equations (the target insight) or solving outright.

SM16L-02.bounds: No free bound. 'a must be negative' follows from the slopes having equal sign, which is the signed-ratio step the subskill names as tested, so it does not reduce the count. The determinant condition 45 + 5a = 0 is the same work.
issues: -9 / 9 is a bare sign pair and -3 is the visible ratio 15/(-5); an options-only solver sees a signed pair plus its factor. Partly unavoidable on this mechanism (every wrong path here is a sign or an inversion of the same ratio), but the +9 could be replaced with a value from an unrelated slip (e.g. 25, from matching the constants instead of the coefficients).

SM16L-03.bounds: Free: the solution set of a linear inequality with n on both sides is a half-line, so the answer is the LARGEST option that satisfies it - that structure makes -4 answerable only if 6, 7 and 9 all fail, which is weak. But it is not a bound: deciding which options satisfy the inequality requires evaluating it. No positivity, divisibility, or magnitude bound applies.
issues: -4 is structurally weak (it can only be the key if all larger options fail), but it is not free-dead

SM16L-04.bounds: Strict reading: 4 survivors - the sign of the perpendicular slope is part of the negative-reciprocal fact the item tests, so charging it would charge the target insight. Recorded reading, and the reason for the repair verdict: the stem's line has NEGATIVE slope, so line k has positive slope, and through (4, -1) with x = 4 > 0 the intercept is -1 - 4m < -1. The key -7 is the ONLY negative option; 4, 5 and 5.5 are all positive. A solver holding the weakest fragment of the tested knowledge - 'perpendicular slopes have opposite signs' - lands on the key without computing 3/2 or substituting the point. That is effectively 1 survivor for a very common half-knowledge state.
issues: Repair: at least two distractors must be negative, so the sign alone cannot decide. Concretely, either add a distractor from the reciprocal-without-the-sign-flip slip m = 2/3 (b = -1 - 8/3 = -11/3) in place of '4' (which is the given line's own intercept and the most obviously foreign option), or move the given point so the correct intercept is positive while the m = -3/2 slip lands negative - e.g. point (-4, 1) gives key b = 7 and the slip gives -5.

SM16L-05.bounds: Reading used: stronger, and stated. |2x - 5| < 11 has an x-window of width 11 (half-width 5.5 about 2.5). Getting the width needs only the single halving step, not the endpoint-strictness decision the subskill declares as the crux, so I count it free. An open interval of width 11 contains 10 or 11 integers. That kills 21 (needs width ~21 - it is the un-halved count, and halving can only shrink) and 7 (a width-11 window cannot hold fewer than 10 integers). Survivors: 10 and 12. Under the strict reading, where the halving is tested work, the count is 4.
issues: thin at 2, and the two survivors differ only by the strict-vs-inclusive endpoint call, so a guesser is at 50% on the tested distinction. Repair: replace '21' with '11' - the off-by-one from counting -3..7 or -2..8, i.e. getting one endpoint's strictness right and the other wrong. 11 sits inside the free width bound, so it survives it, taking the item to 3 survivors and making the endpoint reasoning discriminate three ways instead of two.
